chapter: Long Branch and the war years
title: Jay Peters, a better young tenor than Rouse
summary: Phillips hired Howard student Jay Peters, who read well and later played with Lionel Hampton, taught and died in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Tenor. And played a whole lot of it.
Was he better than Rouse at that time?
Oh yeah, man. He was much better.
He's dead now. If he'd been living, he would.
Oh, he died a couple of years ago. He went to school at Howard. He graduated from Howard when he was 17 or 18. He was a genius, too, you know.
How long did he keep playing music?

He stayed with Lionel Hampton a couple of years. Then he quit, and started teaching. Got tired of traveling. He said he got to teaching. He got some kind of blood disease, and he died -- in Chicago. Nice cat, too. He was only 16 then, but he had the ideas of a grown man. You've seen guys like that. When he was 16 he acted like a man. He sure could play. When he came in there and took Rouse's place, them guys said, "Man, I know you ain't gonna miss Rouse, is you." I said, "No, I don't think so." See, he was way ahead of Rouse. In every way. He was a good musician, too. He could read his ass off then. I mean, any...
Did Rouse ever catch up to him and pass him up? Because Rouse played so much tenor, you know...

Yeah, I guess... Well, see, he's been dead a good while. I don't know how he was playing when he was in Chicago. You see, Chicago was his home. I don't know how he was playing when he died. I think he was just giggin' around Chicago. Because he wasn't playing with nobody. He was just giggin'. I guess he was playing. A cat told me, said he still was blowin', blowin' like hell. But he had the sound like Illinois Jacquet.
I guess Hampton would have wanted that.
He did! He wanted that. Because he took the solos just like Arnett Cobb in Hampton's band.
So he sounds like a good player.
Oh, he was. He was a good player.
